static_traits.name: He Bin
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, keeping a koi named Spot
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with fellow musicians strained due to Self-doubt and not-good-enough feelings; has a few Musician friends but has not yet confided specific unease to them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; never received psychological counseling or treatment in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, Neutral attitude; able to cooperate with exploration and exercises; speech rate and logic details Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I feel people do not take my music seriously, because I also work as an Accountant, which causes Self-doubt and not-good-enough feelings.
basic_info.core_demands: This Self-doubt has affected my music practice and overall mental health; hoping to cope and ease through counseling.
growth_experiences: Since starting careers in both music and Accountant, comments gradually appeared that others think one values Accountant more than music, triggering Self-doubt and inadequacy, repeatedly worsening after interacting with people who question own dedication.

After moving to a new city, facing praise from relatives, friends, or others for artistic performance (like dancing), often subjectively concluding the other is just being polite or does not understand real 'goodness', thus finding it hard to receive positive feedback, gradually reducing investment and motivation.

At Family gatherings, when an aunt praised their performance (dancing), responding politely but inwardly negating the praise, thinking 'she only says this because she is my relative', deepening doubt about self-worth.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of being taken seriously

special_situations.event: Others commenting or implying that having a daytime Accountant job means prioritizing Accountant, questioning their dedication to music
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have a non-music daytime job, others will think I am not serious about music, and thus negate my professionalism
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to seek family and friends' recognition and affirmation, or explain to others her level of investment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am not a professional musician, I am not taken seriously

special_situations.event: After interacting with people who question his music investment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others question my commitment, it means I am not good enough, not professional enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing communication with peers, avoiding talking about unease or downplaying expression
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I am not good enough, then there is no need to try harder

special_situations.event: Being praised by family for their performance (e.g. dancing) at Family gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Praise without objective proof (e.g. awards or authoritative evaluation) does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or ignoring positive feedback, interpreting praise as mere politeness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She is only complimenting me out of politeness

special_situations.event: Sees better performers on TV or online and compares
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach the top level, it means I am not good enough, not worth investing in
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowers practice motivation; avoids performance opportunities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot compare with them, so I am a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be taken seriously, to be recognized as a professional art practitioner (musician/performer)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as unprofessional or not good enough, worrying about being negated and humiliated
defense_goal: Relieving the anxiety of not being taken seriously by seeking external validation
Keeping unease unexpressed, distancing from peers to avoid further questioning

object_relations.self_representation: I am not good enough, an art practitioner easily questioned
object_relations.object_representation: Others are judges/questioners, their praise not sincere

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others praise their performance (e.g. praise at Family gatherings)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding praise as false evaluation out of politeness, believing the other person does not truly approve of them
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a downplaying or self-mocking way, emphasizing 'just being polite', avoiding further exploration of own feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they prioritize accountant work, whether they are truly committed to music
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing others' questions as negation and judgment of self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use objective standards (awards, qualifications) for interpretation, avoid expressing vulnerability and unease, keep a rational and restrained tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about their unease and self-doubt with peers or friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying about being seen as unconfident or as 'fishing for compliments', thus isolating emotions from relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoid expressing inner experience in depth, only give superficial responses or displace the topic, maintain politeness and distance.

manifestations: Living alone but not yet expressing specific unease to music friends
Relationships with peers strained by self-doubt, reducing emotional exchange
outcomes: Emotional support system not yet activated
Decreased sense of self-worth and Increased anxiety

manifestations: When doubting they are good enough, thoughts of 'why bother trying' arise
Negating praise weakens the sense of meaning in their commitment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Worrying about being seen as unconfident or 'fishing for compliments', thus not expressing real unease to friends
Overly focused on how others might evaluate his career choices

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Taking external standards like 'having a daytime job means unprofessional' and 'no awards means not good' as criteria for self-evaluation
Treats others' comments as the basis for determining her own worth

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally directed outward toward himself, restraining expression toward others or seeking support externally.
manifestations: Not seeking support when facing unease and self-doubt, instead repressing emotions
Reduces practice and performance opportunities rather than communicating needs to others

exception_events.target_problem: When their commitment to music is questioned or when comparing themselves, the client usually falls into self-doubt and reduces initiative in practice and performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At a school performance occasion, the client did not avoid it as usual, but accepted the invitation to perform, and received continued invitations and positive feedback.
exception_events.reason: Different support and situation: the formal performance invitation and live audience feedback provided external evidence and support, making it easier to act in the moment and temporarily reducing self-doubt.

positive_force: A certain level of external recognition exists (school performance invitation)
Has a potential support network of music friends
Willing to try reality testing and behavioral experiments, possessing the ability for rational reflection
negative_force: Over-reliance on external validation to determine self-worth
Significant cognitive distortions such as mind reading, catastrophizing, and negating the positive
Difficulty receiving praise and positive evidence, prone to self-denial
Avoiding expressing unease, leaving the support system not yet activated

target_behavior.behavior: Reducing initiative in music practice and performance due to self-doubt
antecedent: Having their commitment to music questioned by others
Making unfavorable comparisons after seeing better performers
Receiving praise but subjectively believing it not genuine
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing about their own professionalism and value, along with mind reading and negating-the-positive cognitive patterns, leads to lowered self-evaluation
target_behavior.function: Escaping possible negative evaluations and feelings of failure, maintaining short-term safety
target_behavior.consequence: Music practice impaired, fewer performance opportunities, tense relationships with peers, sleep and decreased drive

target_behavior.behavior: Habitual speech and thought patterns of negating praise and self-deprecation
antecedent: Being praised by family and friends at Family gatherings or social situations
Being asked about their career commitment and priorities
target_behavior.core_reason: Viewing external polite praise as not genuine, introjecting strict standards and evaluating self in an all-or-nothing way
target_behavior.function: Lowering the anxiety and shame of being exposed as 'not good enough' by preemptive negation
target_behavior.consequence: Finds it hard to consolidate a positive self-concept and motivation, further weakening practice and interpersonal interaction quality
